newsitem.title: UK: New formula helps pick a racing winner - magazine.
newsitem.headline: New formula helps pick a racing winner - magazine.

text.p: Australian animal behaviourists have come up with a six-point plan to help punters pick a winning horse, New Scientist magazine reported on Thursday.
Geoff Hutson and Marie Haskell of the University of Melbourne studied the behaviour of more than 800 horses at two racetracks and compared their demeanour with their performance.
"We reckon that we have six variables that will help the punter recognise a loser," Hutson told New Scientist. "If you could eliminate enough horses, you could bet on the field and come out on top."

According to Hutson, horses should hold their heads at a 45-degree angle, should require no handling before entering the starting gate, should not have to be held tightly when being led around the mounting yard, should have no bandages that could hide an injury and should not carry too much weight.
The odds are also a factor, he said.
"In general, the more relaxed the racehorse, the more chance it had of winning," he said. The research will be published in the journal Applied Animal Behaviour Science.
